title: Nara Park Deer Numbers Hit Record High
paragraphs: Nara Park is famous for its friendly deer, which walk freely among tourists and even bow to ask for food. Now, the number of deer in the park has reached a new record.

In July 2026, the Nara Deer Preservation Foundation, a group that protects the deer, announced that there are now 1,687 deer in and around Nara Park. This was 222 more than the year before, when the number was also a record.

The group counts the deer every year in July. People in the group walk around the area and count the deer they see. They have used the same method since 1953. In 2025, there were 1,465 deer, including 315 adult males, 816 adult females and 334 babies.

Why are there so many deer? According to news reports, one reason is that people are giving the deer food other than special deer crackers. Visitors can buy these crackers, called shika senbei, in the park. They do not contain sugar, and they are safe for the deer. But some visitors give the deer other food, and this may be helping more babies to be born. In addition, the number of foreign tourists has increased again, and many of them feed the deer.
However, having more deer can cause problems. In 2025, the number of tourists who were hurt by deer also increased. For example, deer sometimes bite or kick people, especially when they want food.
The deer in Nara are protected as a natural monument in Japan, so people are not allowed to hurt them. Visitors are asked to be careful when they feed the deer, and to only give them deer crackers.
